A132: STATUS AND KNOWN LIMITATIONS OF THIS VERSION (version label in A1)
A133: Status: this is the final feature version of this sheet. It is frozen: only errors are corrected, each with a new version label and a row on the History of Change(s) sheet; no new inputs, requirements, rules or standards editions are added. Requests for new features are taken for the code version, not for this sheet.
A134: A code version (Python and Rust) is in development. It will take inputs this sheet cannot (e.g., age, breed, whether a nutrient is added as an additive) and will say when a result depends on an input that is not known.
A135: The code version becomes the reference once it reproduces this sheet's published test cases; until then this sheet remains the reference. For its status and the Open Animal Nutrition FHIR Implementation Guide, see https://github.com/openanimalnutrition (openanimalnutrition.org is the planned future address).
A136: Standards: 2006 NRC Nutrient Requirements of Dogs and Cats; 2026 AAFCO Official Publication (Dog and Cat Food Nutrient Profiles); FEDIAF Nutritional Guidelines, September 2025.
A137: The descriptors compare the entered values with the selected requirement's ranges only; they do not show that a diet is adequate, safe or compliant (see the L1 and G1 notes).
A138: A value above a range high reads Highest. The Open Animal Nutrition FHIR IG calls a value excess only above an authoritative max (max types in columns AU to BO of the Healthy Dog Cat Reqt Data sheet; see the E5 note); this grouping is proposed, pending ratification.
A139: Known limitations (this sheet has no input for them; details in the notes named):
A140: 1. Age: FEDIAF Dog Late Growth puppies with an expected adult weight over 15 kg keep the calcium min of 2.5 g/Mcal and the Ca:P max of 1.6 after about 6 months of age, when FEDIAF allows 2.0 and 1.8 (AE52 and AF56 notes on the Healthy Dog Cat Reqt Data sheet).
A141: 2. Breed: FEDIAF's preferred calcium max for Great Dane puppies (1.6% DM) is not applied (B63 note).
A142: 3. Added nutrients: FEDIAF's EU legal maxs for copper, iodine, iron, manganese, selenium and zinc apply only to amounts added as additives, but are applied here to every diet (J3 note on the Healthy Dog Cat Reqt Data sheet).
A143: 4. Sources: iron added as oxide or carbonate and copper added as oxide should not be counted toward the mins (B78 and B80 notes); limits on added selenium and on phosphorus from soluble sources (cats) are not checked (B89 and B67 notes).
A144: 5. Conditional mins: the cat vitamin K and biotin mins apply to every diet, although the standards make them conditional (B102 and B116 notes).
A145: 6. Reference animals: NRC's per kg body weight^0.67 values for kittens and lactating queens apply to one reference animal; this sheet uses them for every kitten or queen (AG3 and AQ3 notes on the Healthy Dog Cat Reqt Data sheet).
A146: 7. Moisture: foods with more than 12% moisture count as wet, a lower cut than FEDIAF's 14% (B40 note); FEDIAF's wet-diet selenium values per kg BW^0.75 (dogs) or BW^0.67 (cats) are not used (B91 note).
A147: 8. Energy density: under an AAFCO requirement, the mins of a food below 4 kcal/g DM are raised to AAFCO's dry matter basis but its maxs stay per Mcal, so it can read above a max it meets on a dry matter basis (C130 note).
A148: 9. Not calculated, only stated in notes: FEDIAF's increase of essential amino acids below 80% protein digestibility and the protein needs of bitches fed little carbohydrate (B12), vitamin E for high PUFA or fish oil diets (B100), vitamin B6 with protein in cats (B112), trace minerals at high calcium (B85), magnesium and urine pH in cats (B76), and processing and storage losses (G1 and B104).
A149: 10. This sheet's own choices where the standards give no value: range highs derived from the min (K1 and K72 notes; Exceptions to Range High sheet), the carbohydrate default min (C124), the energy density range (C130), the energy estimates for the AAFCO requirements (G4 note on the Healthy Dog Cat Reqt Data sheet) and the folate DFE conversion (B114).
